utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think we can bring the witness back in and continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'll remind you of the affirmation you took at the commencement of your evidence; it still applies. And Mr. Whiting has some further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Whiting: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you understand me clearly and hear me clearly?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I first -- with the assistance of the usher, I'd like to return to you the paper you gave at the end of the session yesterday. It was a paper that -- which you used to refresh your recollection as to a specific date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And for the record, we have retained a copy of this paper and provided copies of it to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before you put it back in your envelope, sir, if you could take it back out, just so there is no confusion about the record, could you just -- there just appear to be a few dates marked in 1998. Could you just read what's -- the dates that you -- first of all, did you write this paper? Is this your writing?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I drew them out of some magazines, from the news I heard. They are some data I collected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you write this?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the time. I think it was after the war, right after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could just read the dates that pertain to 1998 -- first of all, what is at the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Special dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there appear to be about four dates at the top pertaining to 1998. Could you just quickly read those for us.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: 28th February 1998, beginning of the war in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next date?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: 25th of July, the offensive in Zborce. 26th July, the murder of -- the killing of Ruzhdi Selihu in Zborce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next date.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: 27th of August, the offensive in Shanuk [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the offensive in Petrastica and Dugel?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there's a number of dates in 1999, but then at the bottom there's some more dates pertaining to 1998. Could you just read those dates, please, starting with 12/10/1998.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the place called Rahi Grunik [phoen] and I was positioned there when the Serb police came. There were about 10 metres away from me and then I attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there is 14/06/1998. What's written beside that date?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first attack in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- and then could you continue reading. The next one is 17...

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: 17 June, the second attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then finally the 23rd of June, 1998, what have you written?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the day of the attack with Molotov cocktails that I mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that all -- you had -- you wrote these dates all down after the war?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write all these dates down before the OTP interview in April 2003?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wrote these dates right after the war. Maybe it was 2000 I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be given a number, and I have a copy. There's no need to take the witness's original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be Prosecution Exhibit Number P120.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to go back and -- you can put that paper away now. I'm going to go back and ask you just a few more questions about your interview with the OTP, and this will go very quickly if you just, please, listen to the questions and answer my questions. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I would ask that the Albanian transcript be put before -- back before the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to confirm with you certain dates -- certain months in the year of 1998 which you say are accurate in the interview, if I could. You said in the interview - and it's on page 6 of the Albanian, and it's on page 14 of the English - that you joined the KLA in April of 1998, and that was accurate, right, it was in fact April 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to page 8 of the Albanian towards the top, and it's page 19 of the English transcript, you stated in the interview that the number of soldiers in your position in -- well, let's say in Kroimire and in Carraleve increased in May and June of 1998, and that's accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 13 at the top of the Albanian transcript, at page 32 of the English transcript, you say that the fighting in Carraleve begins on the 14th of June, 1998. That's accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the date of the first attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what you said in the interview. Right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stated in the interview at page 14 of the Albanian, page 37 of the English, that you were injured in the second attack on the 17th of June, 1998. And that was accurate. You got that date right in the interview. Right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that there was further fighting on the 23rd of June; that's on page 19 of the Albanian transcript, page 46 of the English, further fighting in Carraleve. And that is accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that the offensive in Zborce was on the 26th or the 27th of July, 1998. That's on page 21 of the Albanian transcript; it's on page 48 of the English. That was accurate, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accurate date is the 25th, 26th, this is the accurate date, even though I didn't mention it there. I didn't speak about the 25th. I spoke only about the 26th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you got the second day but not the first day of the offensive in Zborce in the OTP transcript. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during the OTP interview when you gave all of those dates that we've just gone over, they were all correct? Those were all accurate?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's your testimony that when you gave dates on numerous occasions, as many as five occasions, for the headquarters in Klecka and Fatmir Limaj's command over the area around Klecka, you gave dates of spring 1998 or June and July of 1998, it's your testimony, is it, that when you gave those dates that was not correct?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't focus on that General Staff. I said yesterday, I think -- I put it to you that I focused on the year. I didn't know where the General Staff was, but I know that when I received the membership card, then it was Ruzhdi Selihu's battalion. Until then, it was Sokoli 1 and 2 in Petrastica until the battalion was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you gave all these other dates that were accurate, then you were focusing on the month; but when you gave the dates of the command in Klecka, then you were not -- even though you gave months, you were not focusing on them -- on the month that you gave but on the year. That's what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you about what I went through myself. I don't forget these things. Maybe regarding other things, other issues, I might have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm not sure I understand your answer. When are you saying that you forgot?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't focus on the General Staff. I focused on these important dates when I suffered personally in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask that Prosecution Exhibit 119 be put before you again. This is the map that you drew at the OTP interview. And I'm going to draw your attention to pages 22 and 23 of the Albanian transcript; it's page 51 of the English transcript. And yesterday we watched the part of the interview when you drew this yellow line on that map. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't deny that I drew the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember watching the part of the interview when you drew the line yesterday, watching it on the computer? Do you remember watching that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I drew it but I didn't focus on the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm going to draw -- if you would look, please, at page 22 and 23 of the Albanian transcript. And first of all, do you see about halfway down the page, since you've said again that you didn't focus on the time, do you see again about halfway down the page that you -- that the interpreter says that -- talking about July 1998. Do you see that in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe I spoke about it approximately. I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the time. You say about July 1998, and it said the zone under Klecka command. That was your question. The answer is -- I'll tell you now. This is approximately what I am drawing here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. It was -- and you drew approximately the zone under the command of Klecka in July 1998. That's what you didn't, isn't it, approximately?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to page 23 -- and this is -- for the English this is on page 53. Do you see that about one, two, three, four, five, six, seven lines down the page on page 23 in the Albanian, do you see that you say: "There were no companies and battalions then." Do you see that you said that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the line you were drawing was the line of the area before there were companies and battalions. Right? That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know accurately when it fell -- it was under our protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is that what you said there is that the line you were drawing of that area was before -- the area before there were companies and battalions. Right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. Maybe I was wrong, but I don't believe all this part was under the command before the battalions and the zones are formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's exactly what you said in the interview, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave the interview that I was Petrastica with six soldiers at the point. I couldn't cover all that territory with those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not an answer to my question. My question is: You said in the interview that this area was under the command of Klecka before there were companies and battalions. That's what you said, isn't it? Now, if you listen to my questions and answer my questions, we will get finished much more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I was wrong, but the main thing is that this zone before the formation of the battalions and the brigades was not under the Klecka command. Maybe I was wrong. I was not accurate about the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question is not about the time now. It's about that there was a command in Klecka before companies and battalions. And what you said is that Klecka was in command before there were companies and battalions. Are you now telling us that you were wrong about that as well, not just about the dates but about the fact that there was a command in Klecka before there were companies and battalions?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time you said it, you believed it was right, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't focus on the time. I concentrated, rather, on the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The truth is you simply don't want to give the evidence as it is in the interview here today in court because you know or you believe it to be an important issue in this trial. Isn't that the truth, sir?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me it's important to tell the truth because I took the oath to tell the truth. Five years had passed when I gave the interview to you, so some things I had forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this portion continues here, and after you say there were no companies and battalions the interviewer asks you where the staffs where. And you identify a number of places where there were staffs or, shall we say, points, like Kroimire, Shale, Klecka, Carraleve. Isn't that right? Do you see yourself saying that in the interview?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you were saying -- what you said in the interview is that at the time that there were points in these villages, there existed a command over the points in Klecka. That's what you said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I was wrong, but I didn't know that there was a command in Klecka. I knew only that there was a point in Pjetershtice. I knew that there was cooperation, but I didn't know about the existence of a command. I'm talking about April, May, June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said it in the interview, you believed it to be true, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't focus on the time when I gave the interview. I wasn't concentrated on the time, on the month that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- well, I think the record will speak to that, sir. But I will finally ask if you could just -- just turn to page 7 of the Albanian transcript, please, and for the English this is page 17. And I just ask, if you would, to look at the pages -- look over the pages from page 17 -- I mean, I'm sorry, from page 7 to page 30 of the Albanian transcript and just -- you've read this transcript before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but rather late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. But you even found a mistake where it says Nekovce instead of Likovc. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are some mistakes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to take up too much time, but if you could just look from page 7 to 30, and in the English this is page 17 to 81 and just flip through and skim the transcript. Would you agree with me that's what discussed from page 7 to page 30 of the Albanian is the period from when you joined the KLA in April of 1998 to the August offensive in Klecka and everything in between. Would you agree with me? And take a moment just to look at pages 7 to 30 of the Albanian. And again it's page 17 to 81 of the English.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have them in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that right, that from page 7 to 30 it's talking about the time period from your joining the KLA in 1998 -- April 1998; to the fighting in Carraleve in June of 1998; the increase in soldiers in May and June of 1998; your trip to Klecka on the 17th of June, 1998; the -- seeing Isak Musliu and Ymer Alushani in Petrastica; the Zborce offensive on the 26th of July, 1998; and finally the offensive in Klecka in August of 1998. Is that what's covered in those pages, sir in?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that I have said is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is: In those pages, from 7 to 30 in the Albanian, is that -- are those the subjects that it starts with April 1998 and it goes through June of 1998 and July of 1998, and it ends on page 30 with August of 1998. And if you need to take a moment to look at the pages, please do.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, I know these pages. This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in June or July of 1998, did you hear about -- anything about people being taken to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard from some people, but I have not taken their data for granted, to be the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's start with what did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard that some people have been detained, if I have a chance I could give you hear a drawing where the Serbs -- where the Serb forces were there. And I was on the front line, and I know that they stopped people from going to -- from proceeding on their own route, and that's the aspect I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about people being questioned in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, people have been questioned. I have also questioned someone in Lapusnik. He asked, Where are you going and so on and so forth. It was a question of public security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you question someone in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask anyone in Lapusnik but in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Focusing on what you heard -- about you hearing -- what you heard about people being questioned, detained and questioned in Lapusnik, when did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that you didn't hear about that during the war?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm very sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about prisoners being released from Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard of prisoners at Lapusnik. I've only heard where there was an exchange of soldiers with the Serbs; that is a subject I have covered here before you as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when do you say that was?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm given a chance to look at my notes, I've got it noted here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those the same notes that you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you may look at those. And I believe it's Prosecution Exhibit 120.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 23rd of January, 1999, nine soldiers that were being held at the Nis prison were released. And that is what I heard. That was on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about 1998. And did you hear around the end of July about prisoners being released from Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you turn to page 28 of the Albanian transcript. And for the English, this is page 78. I'm going to draw your attention to -- on page 28 of the Albanian, page 78 at the top of the English transcript. About two-thirds of the way down, after there's a little bit of discussion about Holbrooke, and then there's a question about: "Do you know of any detention facilities that the KLA had in the area?" Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you to watch the computer monitor, and we'll watch this portion of the transcript. And if you want to follow the transcript, you may, or you may just watch it on the computer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "D.B.: Yeah, I've heard something of some place -- somewhere, not someplace, but somewhere, but I don't know much. Frankly speaking, from the beginning through the end, I was put into the position that I decide to the area that I was operating along this main road. "O.L.: I understand that, and we're only trying to gather information about what you might know. Do you know if there was possibilities, for example, in Klecka or Kroimire to detain persons? "D.B.: As far as Pjetershtice, Carraleve, and Kroimire are concerned, there's no such a thing as detention facilities. "O.L.: We know that when persons were arrested by the KLA they were usually then handed over by the military police, and the military police would take them to some detention facility. "D.B.: Yeah, that's what I don't know. Where? "O.L.: But you've said you've heard about some place. Can you give us any more information about that? "R.B.: There have been rumours that there was something like that in Lapusnik. I don't know exactly what. As I mentioned before, I've been across a lot of Europe, but not [indiscernible]. As a name, yes, as a name place. "O.L.: Yeah, I'm not asking for anything more. But when did you hear about this place in Lapusnik, for example? Was it ... was it in ... in ... during some incident or how did it come to your knowledge? "D.B.: Yeah, there were rumours circulating that Lapusnik being a place where people were for interrogations, were taken to be interrogated, but that's all I know about this. "O.L.: "Did you hear these rumours during the time when you were holding your places in Carraleve? "D.B.: Yes, as I said, from the beginning to the end as I said in this place. "O.L.: But, I mean, if it's during this time that you heard these rumours? "D..B.: Well, I can't say precisely when, but probably before the first offensive started. "O.L.: Okay. What about then if I can ask you what you heard after the war. Have you heard of -- of course you've heard about Lapusnik then later on. "D.B.: Yes, of course I came to know about Lapusnik due to the fact that Voglushi -- due to his presence there. I knew him earlier, so I knew that he operated in that place. And as I said, he would also come with Qerqiz from this place to -- involved in this Rance. We could also hear shooting -- shooting coming from the direction of Lapusnik because of the fighting going on there. And there were rumours that fighting was going on in Lapusnik. "O.L.: But had you after the war heard about people that had been taken to the -- to the place where they were interrogated in Lapusnik? "D.B.: Yes, I've heard something about that. I've heard that they have been interrogated."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you've seen that, does that remind you that sometime before the first offensive you heard that people were questioned in Lapusnik? Do you remember that now?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it very well. I said that before -- I even asked people where they were going for security reasons and that is the aspect I was focused on because we were on the front line there and Carraleve, and that's the questions we asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew before the first offensive that people were questioned in Lapusnik. Right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you heard that when there was an offensive that there were people released from prison from Lapusnik. Right? You heard that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that after the war. This was -- it was stopped there, but I've heard after the offensive. They were released after the offensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear that at the time of the offensive, that they were released, that these prisoners were released?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. What I said here was that I'd heard after the offensive. Your question was what had I heard after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in response to that question you started to talk about what you heard about Lapusnik during the war, didn't you? And if you need to look at the transcript, you can.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There's no need. After that I started responding to your question of what I had heard after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you see that in fact after that question you started responding to what you heard about Lapusnik during the war and you started to speak about Qerqiz and Voglushi. Isn't that in fact what you said?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after that you said you heard that there were prisoners released at the time of the offensive, there were prisoners released from Lapusnik. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that. I said that afterwards. I said that after the war I had heard what I had heard, to the effect that after the offensive people who were held in prison were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I go into -- could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I finish I would ask to move into evidence the OTP transcript of the interview of this witness, both the English version, the Albanian version, and the video of the interview. If there's a dispute about this, I think it's an issue that perhaps we'll require -- you know, should require further attention. But I don't know that there's any dispute of it going into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there an objection raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We haven't completed the exercise. We only have an interpreter here today, but I have no objection to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There seems no objection, Mr. Whiting. The three items will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number will be P121, and the video will be P121.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I take it P121 is both the English and the Albanian versions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The translation will be P121A.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just so that there's no confusion about this later - and it's not an issue that needs to be addressed now in detail but it's one in fairness that should be flagged - the Prosecution intends to rely on portions of the prior transcript for the substantive value of the evidence. And that is an issue that I'm sure will require a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. certain amount of discussion and perhaps briefing. But I just wanted to -- I didn't want there to be any misunderstanding about that. That is something that we intend to argue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To the extent that it's been adopted by the witness. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, even beyond that, Your Honour. Even beyond that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I expect that your expectation is well-founded then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I appreciate that this is a difficult and complex and perhaps even controversial and I'll even add unfamiliar issue or unfamiliar approach --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps for some.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: -- but we have given this a considerable amount of thought and we think that this position is -- particularly here at the Tribunal, it has a very strong foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, let me say that can be the subject of specific submissions at an appropriate time. At the moment it is received in evidence without objection, but tentative position would be that to be relied on as proof of its content you would need to have that aspect of the transcript adopted as correct by this or some other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tentative position subject to argument, and I'm sure we'll come to learn much more in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. Perhaps when the witness is finished we could discuss the timing of those submissions, whether it's appropriate to do that earlier rather than later. In any event, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mansfield, it's a little early to break, but would it be significantly more convenient to break now or are you prepared to box on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. It would be very convenient because we now do have someone that can interpret, and I value an opportunity to see Mr. Limaj for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you might want 25 or 30 minutes rather than 20?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I would be grateful for that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn until five minutes to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield will now ask you some questions, I expect. Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I thank Your Honours for the time; it's been well-used. We're very grateful. Cross-examined by Mr. Mansfield:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm standing over here. It doesn't matter if you can see me, just so long as you can hear me. I represent Mr. Fatmir Limaj, who sits behind me here, and there's no issue that you met him in June of 1998. Now, I'm sorry to have to ask you some more questions, but I won't take very long about it, hopefully. But I want, if you wouldn't mind, to preface the questions by a little introduction. The questions will be careful, and I will be asking you slowly just to go back to the period between April and August 1998. And in relation to the questions I ask for that period, I will only be asking about your knowledge of various events, places, and people. I am not interested in your belief or your opinion or whatever. Do you understand the difference that I'm seeking to make at this stage?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I go too quickly, please let me know. But I will attempt to keep things chronological for you. And if there's a document that will help you, please let me know. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, firstly I want to ask you about the period between the time that you enrolled or joined up on the 20th of April, 1998, and the time of your first engagement, although you weren't present for all of it, on the 14th of June, 1998. That's the first period.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you registered or enrolled on April the 20th and you've told us that various rules of guidance were read out to you at that time by Luan. Now, I want to go on from that. Were you given your AK-47, your weapon, on the first meeting or did that come later?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first meeting, on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you provided with ammunition to go with it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that date, what did you understand your role was, what you had to do, having been given the weapon?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: My role was to protect the population and the Albanian territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it after the 20th for the purpose of protecting the population that you went to a point in Petrastica? When was it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: After four or five days, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- well, I'll put it simply. The decision to go to that point, was that one you made or someone else made or you made together or how did that come about?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: In corporation with Luan, we decided to be -- that I go to Pjetershtice point with six soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you describe the decision as a collective decision? Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you reached the point, you mentioned there was six soldiers. Did you know the six soldiers before that day?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them, yes, but not everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they came from, those six?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four came from Pjetershtice and I knew them from before. Two came from Mavora [phoen] municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you were in charge. Was that again a collective decision between you and Luan or was it a decision between you and the six soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a decision we made together with Luan. He told me that the best thing for me was to go to Pjetershtice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to be precise. It's not the going to Pjetershtice, it's the being in charge of the point there. Was that a decision made by you and Luan together or by you and the soldiers that you were, as it were, voted to be the leader?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luan and myself, we together made the decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, once you were all assembled, that is you and the six other soldiers, I want to ask you a bit, again in this first period. What did you do most of the time, you seven soldiers at that point, between April the 20th and June the 14th?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time I went illegally to that home, to that house, where we were staying with the soldiers because we didn't know the villagers -- the residents to know that we were soldiers. We didn't want to jeopardise their lives and our lives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this period did the seven of you, first of all, all have any uniform of any kind in this first period?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first period we didn't have any uniforms, but we found some -- I don't know what to say -- some clothes which we used to have -- to make the uniforms. Our wives did the uniforms for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the other six soldiers have weapons for themselves? You had your AK-47, but did they have individually weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: All who were there had weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the weapons of the other six?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this same period, April the 20th to June the 14th, did you have at any time in that period any anti-tank weapons?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any mortars?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 14th of June, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm limiting the periods. So up to the 14th of June you did not have that kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have -- I know it may seem a silly question but I'm going to ask it. Did you have any tanks available to you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We didn't have any tanks, never had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any armoured personnel carriers available to you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any bulletproof clothing available to you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, most importantly I want to ask you this: At your point - again, please remember we'll dealing April the 20th through to June the 14th, I'll come to the later periods - did you have a radio set for communicating?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio set, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where -- there was a small radio set where we were located in that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with whom did you -- was it in your possession or someone else's?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was simply a radio, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply a radio.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a radio set. Not a walkie-talkie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not a walkie-talkie. Did your point have any means of communicating with anyone else other than by sending somebody with a message?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used to communicate through the soldiers, those soldiers that were with us from Pjetershtice. It was through these soldiers that we sent information to Kroimire or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you yourself travel beyond the point where you were stationed; in other words, to other parts of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean during that period, I went several times to Kroimire in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, in this period how much did you really know about what was going on at other points and villages and areas in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to Kroimire to meet Luan, they informed me how the situation was in Komorane. They told me that there was a police roadblock -- checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And anything else?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, would -- at this period still, April to June the 14th, did you know whether Kosovo had been divided up into areas or whether the areas had got names or whether the named areas have got commanders? Did you know any of that at that time, if it had happened?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move closer to June the 14th, the end of this first period. You indicated that on that day you were visiting I think you said your daughter or someone else in another village and you weren't there when the main attack took place. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the point of the attack in Carraleve, and you've done a drawing of the area generally, was the attack completely over?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I reached my position, it was over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discover from the people who were there what had happened?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that there were no injuries on the part of our soldiers and that the clash had been with the Serbian army, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as you could tell, was there damage to people or property on either side, that is your side, protecting Carraleve or on the Serbian side, as far as you knew from what you were told there?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Serbian side, each time they came to assault us, they damaged houses of the villagers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So civilian -- Albanian civilians in Kosovo and in the village were damaged, their houses were damaged, but nobody in the KLA was injured on that occasion. And what about the Serb forces themselves? Were you aware or made aware from the people who were there as to whether tanks had been hit or anything else like that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, three days later, so we're moving into the second period, three days later on the 17th you've described already what happened on that day. But just before dealing with it, do you happen to know how long the engagement on the 14th had lasted?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just over three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the one on the 17th which we're just coming to you indicated last about half an hour before there was a Serb withdrawal. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was injured and half an hour later the withdrawal occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I ask you -- can you estimate then on this occasion how long the engagement as a whole took on this second occasion, 17th?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: On June the 17th the clashes were just over three hours. Half an hour after I was injured I stayed in my position and observed the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated -- I don't want to go back over the detail other than this: You were in one position in Carraleve but there were other soldiers, other KLA soldiers, in other positions on that day. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us, how many other soldiers were in other positions in Carraleve on that day?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the position right in front of me there were three or four soldiers, and I have no idea how many were there in the position where Luan was, three or four but I cannot say a number exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that for this engagement on the 17th of June again, the number of KLA involved were in single figures, in other words under -- nine or under?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only give an exact figure on mine -- on the position that I held, and I cannot be sure about the number of soldiers in other positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just pausing for a moment. Generally up to that point in time, how many KLA soldiers were available to protect the village on a normal day? Three? Six? Nine? Twelve? How many?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say that on the -- on June the 17th there were 12 soldiers in Petrastica. During the attack there were soldiers from Kroimire that took part as well as from other parts who came in to assist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the other soldiers who came in to assist?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only knew Ymer Alushani, Voglushi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of any scheme of plan by which these other soldiers were brought to help you or did you suddenly find they were there?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was only the morale of the army that dictated that soldiers were coming in to assist and die where the need -- where the greatest need was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to describe at this time that the response by the KLA was both instantaneous and spontaneous by people who recognised on the spot that there was a need. Is that a fair description?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 17th, what was the weaponry available to you in your position?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: My own weapon, the AK-47.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any walkie-talkies by now or radio sets for the purpose of communicating with other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never had a walkie-talkie. I've never had a walkie-talkie during the time that I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I won't repeat the question, therefore, each time. So when you were on your own, did you actually fire your weapon at all at the Serbs who were ...

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did. Do you remember whether you hit any of the targets that you were firing at?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was it you hit? Can you remember? Was it people or tanks or ...

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we know you were injured, but can I ask: Do you happen to know - again, I'm concentrating on the word "know," - were there other members of the KLA there with you, was anyone else on your side wounded or injured or killed on that day, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the only one who was wounded. There were no casualties on our side, no other casualties. No one else was injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, so it's clear: There is no issue with you that you met a man called Celiku who you later discover was called Fatmir Limaj, and you went in a car eventually to Klecka. I just want to deal with that. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been to Klecka between April the 20th and this day, June the 17th?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hadn't been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had anyone, in particular Luan or anyone else that you'd spoken to who were part of the KLA, had anyone said to you, Oh, look here, Klecka is the headquarters of a zone which governs the area we are in and there is a commander there called Celiku? Had anybody said anything like that to you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move to the next date you've mentioned, the 23rd of June, because between the 17th and the 23rd you noticed yourself at your point there were more soldiers available, 50 to 60. So I want to deal with that. First of all, the 50 or 60, again did you know some or all of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of them?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at this time with the increase of numbers, what about the weaponry available to these numbers, that is 50 to 60 including, obviously, yourself? What weaponry was then available?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: The major had AK-47 and M-48 rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once again - it's maybe an obvious question and I'm sorry - Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. but what did you understand was the role to be performed by this increase in numbers? What were you all supposed to be doing so far as you were concerned?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that a part of the territory was a greater risk on the part -- by the Serbian forces, and that's why reinforcements came towards the main road that takes to Shtime and Dulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to put it specifically to you -- ask you about it anyway. Was the role purely protective or was it aggressive in the sense that you were to go and look for the Serbs wherever they were?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were interested in the protection of the population to stop the arrival of the Serbian forces to places lime Kroimire and Petrastica, not to go elsewhere and look for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated already on the 23rd of June there was another engagement and there was four of you altogether at your position. Dealing with you first of all and your position, did you have any weaponry beyond the AK-47s and -48s at your position on the 23rd of June?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a Russian sniper weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rrahmani, Rrahman Tafa. He's a martyr now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other weaponry for the 23rd of June?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any other weapons at that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that bottles with petrol, sometimes known as Molotov cocktails, were used. Were these things that you used or soldiers at another position used?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only me and Rrahman used the Molotov cocktails.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When had you assembled the bottles and the petrol ready for use?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: We prepared them earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you? Yes. I appreciate that. But you appreciate you wouldn't want to be running back and forth to a milk crate to get the bottles while it's all going on. So could you help us as to how much earlier you had prepared the bottles with the petrol in? A day before? A week before? Or were they always on hand?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall exactly. But maybe 14, 15 days earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Where were they -- where were they kept? Once prepared, did you keep them in the trenches or the bunker or where did you keep them.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the trenches near the bunker. There was a specific slot for these petrol-filled bottles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And roughly how many do you think you'd assembled ready for use? Can you help there, how many you had ready?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: 25 petrol-filled bottles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 25. And I think you said on this occasion that this engagement as well lasted between two and three hours and that casualties on your side amounted to, is this correct: One person was wounded and two were killed?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I referring to the 17th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, we've moved to the 23rd, the fighting on the 23rd where you used petrol bombs against the tanks which you thought -- I think you've said there may have been up to a hundred tanks in the area generally.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that someone had died or injured on the 23rd. I can't remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Though just dealing with the 23rd for the moment, the day when you use the Molotov cocktails, the 25 bottles, was anybody injured or killed on that occasion on your side?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the occasion where there were two killed and one injured was on the 15th if I'm not wrong then -- and I mean the 15th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 15th of June. Or was it -- because I have a note of what you said before. Or was it the 25th of July?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the 25th of July was Zborce offensive. But before the Zborce offensive there was the clash on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I'll go slowly. There may be a misunderstanding, and I'll take it slowly. On the 23rd, just that day when you used the Molotovs - and forgive me for asking the question again - were any of your soldiers killed or injured on that day, the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any civilians killed or injured on that day, that you know about?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't any over there. There's only damage to the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Only damage to the houses. Now, the wounded and killed that you think was on the 15th, you've just said that, of June, were the wounded and killed on the 15th of June soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: A father and his two sons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A father and the two sons, right. Now, we're coming to the end of this period, in other words the first offensive on or about the 25th of July. It's a date on the list that you have provided to us. So I'm concentrating now on that day, July the 25th, the first offensive. When you took up your position, how many soldiers did you have with you on that day?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: At my position I had four soldiers. To my right, there was another position with three soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So once again, is it fair to say that we're dealing with similar numbers of KLA soldiers, as we have on previous occasions? In other words, very few soldiers in each position?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a large territory -- we didn't have a large territory, so there was no possibility to have more soldiers. And in fact, I felt secure in my role. With only four soldiers, I thought that I'd be able to carry out my responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Did you on this occasion, that is of the first offensive, did you fire your weapons then?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during the first offensive. I only manned my position and waited for them to come up the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use any Molotov cocktails on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not come nearby, near my position. There was no movement there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on this first offensive, as far as you know, was any one of the soldiers fighting with you or who were with you, were any of your fellow soldiers either injured or killed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: On July the 26th, Ruzhdi Selihu was killed and five were injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And civilians?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst the civilians, I think there was a man in Zborce who was killed, and I don't think there were any other casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that it was on the 26th - I hope I have the right date, it may have been the 27th - you constructed a barricade. Do you remember telling us about that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at my notes. To be honest, I haven't checked it with the transcript. It may have been the 27th, yes. But what I wanted to ask you: Whenever constructed, what did the barrack contain? How was it made? What was it made of?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall what kind of barrack. Maybe I've mentioned it, but I can't recall at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, as far as I know you never have mentioned it, as to what it was made of. But did you -- I mean, are we dealing with putting things in a road, whatever you had, a burnt-out car, a tree trunk, old bits of wood? That's the nature of the question, if you can just help as to how you put it together.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the barricades -- I can tell you that on the 14th of June when I went to visit my daughter I asked two or three young men to block the road so that they were not allowed to cross uphill. Whereas, on the 17th we built a barricade just above the school, the old school, so that Serbian forces would not be able to penetrate to a position called Rudina, which was a strategic position and dangerous as far as we're concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Again -- perhaps I can put it this way: Were these barricades that you had put up, for the reasons you've explained, were they makeshift barricades, if that's intelligible?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: With pieces of boulder, with boulder and stones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now, we've got to the end of July and the first offensive. May I pause to summarise, I hope fairly, the position. By the end of July the only weapons you've had have been AK-47s, a Russian sniper weapon, and Molotov cocktails. Is that right first of all -- an AK-48, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think that misstates the evidence. There was also mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I'll come to that in one second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right the weaponry you had? AK-47s, AK-48s, Molotov cocktails, a Russian sniper rifle? Yes?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what we had in our point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, you mentioned much earlier to me when I was going through a list of what you didn't have at various times. By the end of July did you have any anti-tank weapons?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Luan had, but not me in Pjetershtice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I only want to know what you know. You think he did. Did you see any anti-tank weapons in anybody's possession in the group of soldiers that you were cooperating with?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. I'm sorry to be precise about it. Now, I want to deal with mortar weapons. Did you have as far as you know by the end of July any mortar-type weapons?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you by the end of July have any idea how many other villages were involved with the KLA or whether there were any zones or whether there were any overall commanders, in other words a structure of that kind? Had you any idea about that by the end of July?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about any structures. I knew that the points were increasing in cooperation. They kept increasing with every passing day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated yesterday that -- and the day before that the time at which you now recall that you knew about those structures was once brigades and battalions had been formed, and you mentioned the date in August. Do you recall saying all that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I have some questions about this area. Before you gave your evidence to this Tribunal, started giving your evidence, is it right you had a meeting with the prosecuting counsel, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? Can you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Before you came into this courtroom for the first time at the beginning of this week, did you -- before that moment, had you already had a meeting or conversation with Mr. Whiting, counsel for the Prosecution who's asked you questions over these last few days?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I may have the identity wrong. Did you have a meeting -- I've got the name right this time, but the wrong person. Did you have a meeting with any lawyer representing the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. With the exception of Mr. Alex, that is, Mr. Whiting and Ole, I didn't meet anyone else, didn't talk with anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If I can assist, it was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's interesting that you're not regarded as a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's not that, it's I'm Mr. Alex.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Mr. Alex. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, now we have Mr. Alex in our focus. I just wanted to ask you when you had your meeting with Mr. Alex and someone else, what did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me what is recorded, but I didn't focus on the time period about which he asked. Some things I had forgotten. Five years had elapsed by that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated to us that because of that time lapse you needed certain documents, and you've produced a card, Exhibit 117, and now a list, Exhibit 120. But you also indicated there were other documents. I just want to ask you: Are there other documents that help in your recollection that we don't have yet?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have some at home, but I'm very certain that the brigades and the battalions were not called after living persons. So I'm certain that Ruzhdi Selihu who was killed in July, Kumanova in August. It was after their killing that the battalions and brigades were named. This is what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just one more question about the question of notes. Did you keep notes in 1998 about your experiences and what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something I had more, but they were burned. But I have some yet. I can't tell you how much notes I have. I haven't looked at them after the war myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to ask you to speculate unless you know. If you don't know what the notes contain that you still have. Are they at your home back in Kosovo or somewhere? Are the notes still somewhere in a briefcase or a drawer or what?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have them in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can I ask it this way: What were you noting down? Do you remember what you were noting down in 1998? What sort of things would you write down, whether the notes exist or have been destroyed?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like here, for example. You saw those dates, important dates, for me. I have some other notes like these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any other notes with you? Because we've all seen you've had a -- what seems like a little file to your left-hand side. Does that contain other notes than the ones we have here?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have photos and some permissions which allowed us to circulate. I have some orders to operate -- I received then, to do something, to operate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you shown this file to anyone from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have an opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I said at the beginning: If you need to look at any of the notes to help you answer any of these questions I'm asking, please feel free to do so. Now, I want to move from the end of July into August, and as you've indicated the formation of brigades named after -- or battalions in particular named after people who were martyrs. When was it after the date on the card that you've indicated, when was it after that that you discovered anything about the way the army was being organised?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the organisation, but I know that as of August the name was given to our battalion, Ruzhdi Selihu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I ask it this way: Beyond the name relating to your battalion, did you know how many other battalions there were mid- to late August 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know how many brigades there were mid- to late August?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether there were any particular zones, if that's what they were called, after about the middle to late August 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there came a time when civilians, to protect them, were taken to valleys or gorges where they could be safe from attack. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself help with that process?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I helped in any way I could. I never spared any efforts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm only asking about what you know about this as well. Could you estimate from your personal experience roughly what numbers of civilians were being shepherded into the gorges or valleys for protection?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you ask me about Petrastica, during the first offensive there were about 5.000, 7.000. I was fighting in the front line, and the gorge was arriving [as interpreted] people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you appreciate there were more numbers after that later or are those the only ones you knew about?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later their number grew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "later," when do you mean later?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an accurate time, but the most important part where people were shepherded was when the Serb presence was greater. They said there was an estimation that up to Komorane there were over 75.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you can -- just going back to the position with the battalion you were in from August onwards, by that time were you yourself provided with a uniform, mid-August onwards?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the time when they gave me the uniform, the important thing being that I had a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Can you help us as to, again, the weaponry you had available after the second offensive and after the formation of your battalion? Sorry, my fault. It is a question, badly put. What weaponry was available to you and the soldiers you served with in the battalion after the middle of August 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same weapons. One mortar, 500 I think, we received it after August with three shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say you received it, do you mean you in a little unit or what?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some comrades went to Albania, they got arms and came. They came -- they were from Zborce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other weaponry besides obviously rifles and a mortar with three shells? Anything else?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kalashnikovs. Some others came with their own weapons; they had bought them somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, only have one more question; it relates to a conversation with Fatmir Limaj, Celiku as you knew him, on the way to Klecka. Is your recollection that he said to you that you should be careful with the civilian population and that they should be protected at all costs? Did he say something like that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I have no other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mansfield. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolski. Cross-examined by Mr. Topolski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I represent Isak Musliu and I have a few questions for you. Isak Musliu you knew in the war as Commander Qerqizi. That is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw him, as you have told us, sometime in June with Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Voglushi?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to follow the same order of questioning that Mr. Mansfield just did. My questions will not repeat his, I hope, therefore please be patient with me while I ask them. I want to start before the war. You came back to Kosovo, am I right, in May of 1997?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us when you began your evidence in this courtroom a couple of days ago that you had problems with the Serbs, that you had been arrested and beaten at a police station in Shtime. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand it correctly that the allegation against you related to the possible holding of a firearm, was that the allegation they made against you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have heard much in this case and no doubt will hear more about houses being searched for firearms. I want to see if we can understand the position clearly. Before the war in 1997 were Albanians permitted by the Serbs to have firearms in their homes?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in those cases when they cooperated or collaborated with the Serbs, otherwise not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You needed, did you not, a certificate to hold a firearm in those days?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only people who could provide such a certificate were the Serb authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
