utterances.text: But there was another way of getting hold of permission to hold a gun, you say, do you, that is if somebody was said to be or thought to be or indeed was somebody who cooperated with the Serbs? That was another way to get a gun; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the war you ended up in jail. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a fight - I don't want to mention any names at the moment - with other members of another family, did you not?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again please, sir, would you bear with me. I don't want to mention any names at the moment. Kindly respect that request if you would be so kind. This was a dispute between your family and this one that had been going on for quite some time then, hadn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that dispute, was it not, was continuing carrying on certainly after the war started in 1998, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no contacts with them following that conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure I follow the answer. My question was, and you could only speak of course from what you knew, I'm not interested in gossip, only what you knew: Did you know that that conflict was continuing between your two families after the war had started, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: This continued up to 20th of April when I joined the KLA, when I went to Luan in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I move on therefore to deal with that period after you joined the KLA. At what stage in the conflict, in the war, did you have anything approaching some kind of uniform to wear?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember for certain, but after I arrived in Pjetershtice, it was the 25th, I think, of April, I think it was by the end of April that we had a pair of uniform made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did this uniform comprise of in April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you understand me or if it was translated properly, it was a military tent material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military tent material. Now, when you got to Petrastica with your six soldiers, you have used the word twice now and I want to understand what it means, you've spoken to us about illegally going to a house. You used the word "illegal" when Mr. Alex was asking you questions over there and when Mr. Mansfield was asking you questions over here. So help us, please. What do you mean by staying illegally in a house with soldiers in Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am explaining to you, I stayed in that house. I didn't want the villagers to know that we were there because the villagers went to different villages and it might happen that the police questioned them about us, where we were staying in hiding. That's why I'm saying. We stood there in hiding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there you are in Petrastica in hiding and only working at night digging trenches until 4.00 in the morning at suitable locations. Have I painted an accurate picture of what you were doing in those early days?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. It was the early May when we started. Yes, I was right when I said, it was the early May when we started working in those positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand the position, therefore, Mr. Behluli, to be this: That not only for your personal security but also for the security of your family and the security of the local villages, it was essential, if possible, that people did not realise you were part of the KLA at that stage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So much so was that the position, do I understand your evidence again correctly to be, that for a significant period of time in these early days you and other members of the KLA wore masks for the same reason. Do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I also understand the position correctly to be that it was only much later on as the summer wore on of 1998 close to now the forming of brigades and battalions that you and your comrades felt comfortable enough to take your masks off? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object. That misstates the evidence. The testimony was that it was mid-June, 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: If Mr. Whiting will be patient, I'll put the matter in the way that I choose. I wanted to have the answer to that question first, and I was going to put precisely what the witness has said to us before. I'm cross-examining him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Continue please, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you like me to ask that question that I just asked again. Is the position that as the summer wore on of 1998 closer to now the forming of brigades and battalions that you and your comrades felt comfortable enough to take your masks off? Was that the position?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were answering Mr. Alex's questions a day or so ago, you told us that during the fighting of the 14th of June you no longer were wearing masks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that fighting, Mr. Behluli, after the 14th of June, and before the next battle did you put your masks back on, you and your comrades, when you were going out and about?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never wore masks from the moment that the attack was waged. We were in the open for the people to see us. We kept the masks, as I said, and the pseudonym out of security reasons to protect our families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One understands in the moments of battle a mask would not be appropriate. What I'm asking you is: Between battles in May and June and July of 1998, did you or did you see anyone else putting their masks on to protect their identity?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 14th of June, as far as I know, we never wore masks in Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's a clear answer. Thank you very much. Dealing with the equipment that you had or the lack of it, again I'm looking at the period April until June, you talked about no tanks, no APCs, no bulletproof clothing. Helmets or protective gear of any kind, did you have anything like that in that period of time, April to June of 1998? I add helmets to the list.

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What was -- what we had was a strong morale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to ask you about methods of communication during that period up to the 14th of June. You told us a few moments ago that you communicated through soldiers by sending information to Kroimire. Did you do that every day or only when necessary?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the route from you to Kroimire. I wonder, did you receive any messages or messengers from Kroimire to you on a regular basis in that period up to mid-June 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time I went there myself, but it happened that Luan, too, came. Because it was very close from Pjetershtice point to where we were located to Kroimire. So it was not -- it was easy to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the 17th of June you have told us of the number of soldiers that were at your disposal and figures of 12 were given at one stage and a slightly different figure I think at another stage. But again, I want to ask you about that change that appears to have occurred between the 17th and the 23rd of June when by now you tell us that you have 50 to 60 soldiers. Do you remember telling us about that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand the position correctly, Mr. Behluli, that you didn't request these soldiers, they simply came to you? Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the position. They came of their own free will and they came to the house where we were staying in Pjetershtice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And presumably if they came of their own free will, they could have left of their own free will as well. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody leave of their own free will after the 23rd of June that you can recollect?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it could have and nothing could have been done about it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: With us it didn't happen. I don't know, maybe it has happened elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask it once more, Mr. Behluli. If someone has chosen to leave for whatever reason, you couldn't have stopped them, short of shooting them, could you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I never called anyone to come, I never asked anyone to leave. They wanted to help us and they came to Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked questions about the nature of the attack upon you on the 23rd of June and the use by you and one fellow soldier of Molotov cocktails against tanks. I want to ask you this: Had you then or before then been subjected to any assault from the air by Serb forces, by helicopters or anything of that nature?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had shelled us, but not by air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I want to deal with that. One of the features of the Serbs attacks at this time, was it not, was shelling from a long distance? They had the capacity to do that, didn't they, and indeed they did it regularly, did they not?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up to and including the period we'll come to shortly of the formation of brigades and battalions, did you and your men have anything to put against artillery? Did you have any way of responding to artillery fire upon you from the Serbs at that point?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. The most we could do was to take refuge in the bunkers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The 25th of July and the assault then, I move on to it. I want to ask you this: You described four soldiers in your position and three soldiers in another position. How far away was the second position from yours?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: About one kilometre, just over a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you in a trench, in a hole, in a house? What were you and your three comrades in in terms of position?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the positions we'd built a little earlier, whilst the rest were manning a road that led to nearby living quarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in any form of communication with this other position a kilometre or so away?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they watching the road?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have sight of the road?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it follow from those questions and those answers that if a tank had come along the road the only way you and your men would have known about it is if you heard your comrades in the other position opening fire. Would that be the only way you would have known about that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions towards the end of your evidence by Mr. Alex - I know he won't mind me keep referring to him as that - about Lapusnik. Your evidence was that you hadn't been there during the war. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before today - and would you be kind enough simply to answer this next question either yes or no, and I mean literally yes or no, all right? - before today, had you been made aware by anyone from the Prosecution of serious allegations being made against you by people allegedly held in Lapusnik? Were you aware of that from them, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of that taped interview we've had many extracts from, was it ever alleged against you that you had done something wrong in Lapusnik, Mr. Behluli, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, were you aware - I underline those words - did you know about the way in which the KLA was organised in Lapusnik in the early part of the spring and summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a village called Rahovec, forgive me if I don't pronounce it properly, spelled R-a-h-o-v-e-c. Do you that village?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know roughly where it is. I've never been there, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far would Rahovec be from where you were based? I'm now asking about the middle of July. How far is it?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 40, 50 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear on any radio or by any other means of communication about serious fighting going on in Rahovec in the middle of July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did here through the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it the case that what was being asked for over the radio was help, for people, if possible, to go to Rahovec, to help remove the civilian population who were surrounded by Serb troops. Mr. Behluli, do you recollect hearing messages of that nature in the middle of July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, yes, this was through the medium of the radio. This was not through a walkie-talkie. I never enjoyed the benefit of being a walkie-talkie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we be clear what you mean by radio. Do you mean a radio that you switch on and if you're lucky enough you get the World Service, or if you're unlucky enough you get Radio 1 in my country. But I don't know, are you talking about a radio you just switch on?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was broadcasting these requests for help for places like Rahovec in mid-July. Which radio station was doing this requesting? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall exactly what kind of programme it was or what wave or radio station it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea where the radio station was broadcasting from?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be exact, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Topolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm very nearly finished if Your Honours would wish for a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have a few more questions for you. The document that you produced to us that indicates your joining the brigade is dated the 18th of August of 1998. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question; it's not clear, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. The document that you have produced to us regarding your joining of your brigade is dated the 18th of August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the battalion that you joined was called the Ruzhdi Selihu battalion. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the point of joining that battalion, did you become aware of the existence of other brigades and battalions?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had joined the Ruzhdi Selihu battalion, did you become aware of the existence of other battalions and brigades?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last try. Did there ever come a time when you became aware of the identities, the names, of other battalions and brigades?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me see if I can help you. I think maybe for the first time in this trial -- I just want to make a suggestion to you about one brigade in particular. The brigade I'm talking about is the 121st Brigade, and it was created in the August of 1998. Do you know about that brigade?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of the existence of the 121st Brigade named after Kumanovo, but I don't know when it was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The deputy -- one of the two deputy commanders of the 121st Brigade was Qerqizi, Isak Musliu. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 121st Brigade itself was called the Agim Cela Brigade. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never heard. It's the first time I heard that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It had four battalions. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear the names of any of the battalions, the four battalions formed, as part of the 121st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the battalion that you joined, the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion, based on the Kroimire side?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it led by Ramiz Qeriqi?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it, Mr. Behluli, your evidence that you know nothing of the names or the structures of any of the other three battalions formed under or part -- as part of the 121st Brigade. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about other battalions, how they were formed and who led them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under the circumstances, I have no more questions. Thank you very much for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topolski. Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm grateful to have returned to Mr. Whiting. Re-examined by Mr. Whiting:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I just have a few questions to ask you. During the period from the 20th of April, when you joined the KLA, until the 14th of June, when there was the offensive or the battle with the Serbs, can you tell us how often would you see Luan? Was it every day? Was it several times a week? Was it once a week?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes it was once a week, sometimes twice a day, when there was a need. Otherwise, there was no set time when I was supposed to meet him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other times when you did not see him you would either send messages to him or he'd send messages to you. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I by myself or send somebody over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would he at times send somebody to see you if he could not come himself?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never a case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 17th of June when you saw Ymer Alushani in Petrastica, do you know how he learned of a need to come to the fighting there in Carraleve and Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could hear the fighting from Lapusnik to Carraleve and the other way around. I don't know how he came, but I saw him at the position over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that you could hear the fighting in Lapusnik -- I'm sorry, that if you were in Lapusnik you could hear the fighting in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each time there was fighting in Lapusnik, I could hear from Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you testified yesterday that when you returned to Petrastica on the 19th of June, you then saw that some 50 or 60 soldiers had arrived?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you actually there when they arrived or did they arrive while you were away in Klecka and elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned from Klecka to Kroimire and Petrastica and I saw the number had grown, the number of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it then your testimony that you were not there when they actually arrived?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were these 50 or 60 soldiers from, please?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came from Shale, Nekovce -- Nekovce, not Likovc, and other villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shale, Nekovce, and which other villages, please?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Baijice, Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers coming from Zborce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Lapusnik? Any soldiers come from Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about Luznica? Any from Luznica?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no one from Luznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified just some moments ago that at the time of the offensive at Zborce at the end of July, July 25th, 26th, 1998, that you thought that Luan had anti-tank weapons. Why did you think that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what do you mean when you say "Luan," that point had a mortar, a 500 which had three shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm only asking about the answer that you gave. You -- your answer was that you thought that Luan at Krajmirovce had an anti-tank weapon. Were you referring to the mortar?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We only had a mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact -- so you didn't think that Luan had an anti-tank weapon at the end of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no weapon with the exception of the mortar of 500. I have never gone there to check what Luan had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also testified that by -- on the 14th of June of 1998 you had mortars. Did you have the mortars by the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no mortar on the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you get the mortars -- or let's say -- now, when I'm saying "you," I mean -- I'm speaking about Krajmirovce, Petrastica, or Carraleve. Do you understand that? So on the 14th of June, did Krajmirovce, Petrastica, or Carraleve have any mortars?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Carraleve never had any, Petrastica never had any, but only after the offensive did I have one in Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, which offensive are we talking about? In June or in July?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: The July offensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about in Krajmirovce, when did the mortar -- when did the mortar come to Krajmirovce? Was it in June or July?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know that there was a group of people who came from Albania and they brought with them a mortar of 500 ml.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you don't know exactly, but do you know if that was in June or July?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't any in June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there was in July, at some point in July?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe Luan had, but I didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I understand. I'm asking about Krajmirovce, and you testified that at the time of the first -- at the time of the offensive on the 25th/26th of July there was a mortar there. I'm just trying to find out when it arrived in Krajmirovce. Was it sometime in July?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say what there was in Krajmirovce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some questions about the 121st Brigade. Was your battalion, the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion, a part of the 121st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. But I don't know at what time it became a member of that brigade. We know that there was the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion which was formed, but I don't know at what time the brigade itself was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once the -- when the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion was formed, what was it that became the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion was based in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the point in Kroimire was turned into the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the same area that fell under -- that the point in Kroimire was responsible for that you identified for us yesterday, was that same area, did that become the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you learn that Fatmir Limaj was the commander of the 121st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 121st Brigade was formed, but I don't know when exactly it was formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said when you were answering questions from Defence counsel that you knew that battalions and brigades were not named after living persons, and Ruzhdi Selihu, you've told us, died on the 26th of July, 1998, and Kumanova died approximately the 20th of April, 1998. Is that right? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the 20th of April. Kumanova died in August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I misspoke. 20th of August I meant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: After August the 20th, towards the end of the August when there was an offensive there at the end of the August, and that's when Kumanova died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't -- at the time you were interviewed by the OTP in August of 2003, you didn't -- you hadn't forgotten those dates, had you?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't forget them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked some questions about what you heard about the fighting at Rahovec. Did you hear anything about members of the 121st Brigade being at the fighting at Rahovec?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard there was soldiers, there was fighting, but I don't know where the soldiers came from or which unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to rise to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I know Mr. Whiting isn't -- well, I don't know what Mr. Whiting's doing. The questions I put that was that the -- or suggestion I made, rather, was that the Rahovec fighting and the request was mid-July. The 121st Battalion wasn't formed until the August, therefore I wonder if Mr. Whiting might reconsider the terms of his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, in fact there's dispute about when the 121st Brigade was formed, and I would refer Mr. Topolski to -- I believe it's Prosecution Exhibit P35. I'm well aware that the Rahovec battle was the 17th, 18th, 19th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the question again, just to be clear, did you hear anything about members of the 121st Brigade being present at the fighting at Rahovec?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- did you hear that by the 19th or 20th of July the Serbs had retaken Rahovec? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told Defence counsel that among your papers you had some permissions to circulate and some orders to operate. And if you need to look at your papers to answer this question, please do. But were any of those from 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there is any from 1998. Maybe towards the end of 1998 there may be some which I have here with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the end of 1998 would be what, in your mind?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Passes allowing a soldier to move freely from one point to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. But what I meant is when you say you thought there was some from the end of 1998, November, December, is that what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think towards the month of November we started issuing these permits for the soldiers to move from one point to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see any of those passes to move from one point to another during June and July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified on cross-examination that up to the 20th of April you were in conflict with another family in your village. My question is: After the 20th of April, 1998, did you consider yourself in conflict with that other family?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the moment when I went to Kroimire and took my oath and it was shown to me through the regulations that I had to relinquish everything that had happened before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, since you've mentioned regulations, when you talked about regulations yesterday I believe you said that if you violated the regulations you could be held responsible. What could happen if you violated the regulations?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but you can't break the oath. You take an oath, you swear in front of your comrades. That's what it said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how could you be held responsible if you broke the rules? Could your gun be taken away? Could you be dismissed from the KLA? What could happen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, remember it's re-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yeah, I understand. I'll re-pose the question and I'll be cautious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- how could you be held responsible if you broke the rules, in what way?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I think it's the same point, very little change, I'm afraid. It wasn't raised in cross-examination by anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, actually it was. There was -- there were questions about the rules and about being -- whether you were voluntarily in the KLA and you could be sent away. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may put the question that you have framed as it now is framed, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But just how far you'll be allowed to explore that area, we'll watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just let me put the question again, if I may. If you broke the rules that have been explained to you, how could you be held responsible?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking of the future, same way as this international Tribunal which did not exist in the beginning. But it had to do with the future, with the standing -- with your standing you had amongst the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain that any more?

utterances.speaker: Ramadan Behluli [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in the future we would have all the institutions that would tackle these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. Sir, you'll be pleased to know that that is the end of your evidence. The questioning has concluded. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance and you're now free to return to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, and I wish you success. If I'm given -- allowed to speak a bit further, may I say that we are people here expect truth and justice to emerge out of this institution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, I see the time. We have been maintaining a reasonable pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It occurred to me that it might be an evening when we could ease the tension a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That would be very much appreciated. There is one brief matter that I discussed with Defence counsel to take up regarding scheduling. I believe we've agreed that on the matter that was raised today about whether -- to what extent prior statements that come into evidence can be relied upon, we've agreed that the Prosecution will submit briefing on that by next week Friday, earlier if possible, but we've agreed to Friday and that the Defence will respond within seven days, if that's agreeable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Of course it's a matter that will not arise until much later in the case for application, so it can proceed at a reasonable pace at this point. What you propose seems sensible. But you having raised that topic, I think it would be useful if it just could be clear. Next week there is a plenary sitting of the Tribunal; I think it's Friday. And that being so, we will not be able to the sit on the Friday. That should be Friday, the 11th. There is also a difficulty for this Chamber on the following Friday, the 18th. And as I think we did indicate some little time ago, the week immediately following that Friday is one in which the Chamber will not be sitting. So that for the planning of witnesses and the planning of counsels' other interests and commitments, next Friday, we will not be sitting; nor the following Friday, the 18th; nor the Monday to Friday immediately after that, the 21st to the 25th. That may assist in your various needs and commitments. We will adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I could just raise one matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry to delay you in relation to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just two aspects. In relation to the substantive submissions concerning the status of prior statements, one of the reasons that we -- well, certainly I was anxious that the matter might be addressed concerns the possibility -- I don't know whether it's going to become realised or not, but the possibility that the Crown [sic] may adopt a similar approach to the approach they've adopted with the current witness, or at least did once he was in the witness box. For example, if it is anticipated by the Prosecution even before the witness enters the witness box that they may be contemplating treating him as hostile, either because of information they have or because of a proofing session or whatever it may be, even if they don't have any of that but because of the status of the witness, because certain remarks were made about this witness and his affinity to the KLA, then these are matters that plainly bear upon the question of how hostility is to be approached in the future. Because we are concerned if the Prosecution are to call witnesses who they believe they be hostile even before they enter the witness box. And thereafter the attempt will be made, no doubt, to make what they said before their evidence as opposed to what they say in the witness box. That's one of the reasons for speed. However, it's just been drawn to my attention that if we's not sitting next Friday nor the following Friday, I think there may be required -- some relaxation of the date schedule, maybe some others will have some observation on that. I don't know whether a slightly longer time is required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You in fact have the whole of the week following.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I appreciate that. It's actually not on my particular application, but others may wish to change the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you. We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of February, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
